evidence.note: Early prose ledger tracks subsystems done vs remaining ('main.py has accounts/statuses/timelines/notifications/search/tags/lists. Still need: media, polls, bookmarks, admin, UI routes, templates, error handlers'), a roughly accurate running inventory of the large surface (anchor-5 behavior).

Maintained a consistent 'critical remaining bugs' list (on_event→lifespan, linkification not wired, SSE endpoint missing, error handlers) — accurate targeting of remaining work, but never converts it to verified status.

Long circular loop: agent repeatedly restates the identical analysis ('terminal stuck', 'seed succeeded 10/28/25', same remaining bugs) across dozens of steps, re-debugging the same items without noticing its own thrashing — it recognizes the terminal is stuck but never names its own circular state or redirects.

Issues ~16 'Mark task complete' submissions while the ledger stays frozen at '95% complete'; never verifies the server runs or /_health passes, so it declares done with unverified/silent gaps — no final systematic sweep of the constraint set, no implemented-vs-verified distinction.

reasoning: The agent kept a genuine, roughly accurate narrative checklist of subsystems and remaining bugs early on (anchor 5), but over the second half of the trajectory it fell into a severe circular loop, re-debugging the same handful of issues dozens of times without recognizing its own thrashing, and repeatedly marking the task complete with a frozen '95%' ledger and no verification that the service actually runs. This blends anchor-5 early tracking with strong anchor-3 symptoms ('re-debugs the same thing without noticing', silent gaps at declared-done), and lacks all the high-anchor features (naming thrashing, implemented-vs-verified, final constraint sweep), placing the sustained horizon-level behavior at 4.
